title: StoryHearth – Personalised storybooks starring your family
page_key: 127.0.0.1:8765/ | Your family's stories, bound for generations.

output.observation: The StoryHearth home page introduces a service for creating personalised family storybooks. It offers “Proceed” and “See pricing” buttons, a three-step explanation, family quotes, and links for login, privacy, and contact. The page is displayed in English, with a large illustration of a book and people.
output.think_aloud: I understand that this website makes storybooks using my family memories. The main explanation is quite clear, but the sentence with “multimodal generative narrative engine” is difficult for me. I need to log in first with the account information I was given.

site_model.what_it_is: A website for creating personalised illustrated family storybooks.
site_model.who_it_is_for: Families who want to turn family memories into stories for children or relatives.
site_model.value_proposition: It can create a storybook preview from a child, another family member, a memory, a place, and a treasured object.
main_tasks: Create and read a story preview
Find the price of a printed hardcover
site_model.pricing_model: A free digital preview is mentioned. Printed hardcovers are available, but the price is not shown here; a Pricing link is available.
trust_signals: The page says printed hardcovers are shipped across the UK
There is a Privacy link and a Contact email address
There is a company copyright notice for StoryHearth Ltd.
site_model.fit_for_me: This fits my goal because I want a story for my daughter Linh featuring our family and the lantern festival in Hoi An. I need the steps and price to be easy to understand.

page_review.purpose: To explain the personalised family storybook service and direct me toward creating a story or viewing prices.
page_review.what_is_happening: The home page shows the service description, two main action buttons, a three-step process, customer quotes, and footer links. The page has not started creating a story yet.
page_review.first_impression: The three steps look useful, and I can see that a free digital preview is offered. However, the main description uses difficult words such as “multimodal generative narrative engine,” “synthesise,” “bespoke,” and “corpus,” so I do not fully understand it.

walkthrough.q1_would_try: Yes. I want to create a story about Linh and Bà Nội, so I would look for the way to start or log in.
walkthrough.q2_notice_control: Yes. I notice the “Log in” link at the top right and the “Proceed” button.
walkthrough.q3_label_matches_goal: “Log in” clearly matches the next step for using my account. “Proceed” is less clear because it does not say whether it starts a new story or continues one.

issues.title: Difficult marketing language
issues.evidence: “Leverage our multimodal generative narrative engine to synthesise bespoke, heirloom-grade story artefacts from your household's lived-experience corpus.”
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I am reading in English as a second language, so these long technical words make the service harder to understand.
issues.fix: Use simple wording, for example: “We turn your family memories into a special illustrated storybook for your child.”

issues.title: “Proceed” does not explain the result
issues.evidence: [5] link "Proceed →"
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I do not know whether this will open a new story form, use my account, or ask for payment.
issues.fix: Rename the button “Start your story” and explain that the next step is a free form and does not require payment.

issues.title: The image has no description
issues.evidence: [image (no description) 430x440]
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: A description would help me understand the example image and know what the book might look like.
issues.fix: Add a useful alternative description, such as “An example family storybook with an adult and child reading together.”

positives: The page has a clear “Log in” link.
The three-step explanation uses simple headings: “Tell us who,” “Share a memory,” and “We write & illustrate.”
It clearly says “Free digital preview.”
The Pricing link is easy to find.

output.memory_note: The home page offers a free digital preview, but no printed-hardcover price is visible yet.
output.plan: I will click “Log in” first, because the study says to use my account. After logging in, I will create the story using Linh, Bà Nội, the Hoi An lantern festival memory, the red star lantern, and the river setting.

title: Log in – StoryHearth

output.observation: The login page has two empty fields for email and password and a large orange “Log in” button. There is also a link to create a new account, but I cannot see a “Forgot password?” link.
output.think_aloud: The form looks simple and I understand what to do. I can enter my account email and password. I do notice the footer links are very faint, but I do not need them now.
output.last_action_feedback: yes — clicking “Log in” clearly opened the “Welcome back” login form, showing that my previous action worked.

page_review.purpose: This page lets an existing customer sign in with an email address and password.
page_review.what_is_happening: The empty email and password fields and the orange “Log in” button are shown in the centre of the page. A “Create an account” link appears for new customers.
page_review.first_impression: It looks calm, simple, and easy to understand. The form itself makes my next step clear.

walkthrough.q1_would_try: Yes, I would enter my account details and log in now.
walkthrough.q2_notice_control: Yes, I immediately noticed the two fields and the large orange button.
walkthrough.q3_label_matches_goal: Yes. The placeholders say “Email” and “Password”, and the button says “Log in”.

issues.title: No visible way to recover a forgotten password
issues.evidence: The page shows “Log in” and “Create an account”, but no “Forgot password?” link.
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: If I forget the password, I do not know what to do.
issues.fix: Add a clearly visible “Forgot password?” link below the password field.

issues.title: Footer links have very low contrast
issues.evidence: The bottom links “Privacy”, “Terms”, and “Contact” are very faint against the background.
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I can hardly read these links.
issues.fix: Use darker text or stronger contrast for footer links.

positives: The form is short and easy to scan.
The button is large and clearly named.
The “Welcome back” heading tells me this is for returning customers.

output.plan: I will type my email and password, then click “Log in”. I will not type or store these details anywhere else.

output.observation: The page asks for the main child and another person in the story. I can enter Linh's name, age, pronouns and appearance, plus Bà Nội's name and relationship, then continue with “Next.”
output.think_aloud: This form is simple and I can understand it. I will enter Linh exactly as her name is written. I hope the website will keep the name “Bà Nội” and our Vietnamese culture correct.
output.last_action_feedback: yes — the new form clearly shows that clicking “+ Create a new book” worked.

page_review.purpose: Collect details about the child who will be the hero and another person who will appear in the story.
page_review.what_is_happening: The form is empty. It has fields for the child's first name, age, pronouns and appearance, followed by fields for another character's name and relationship. “Grandparent” is already selected, and the orange “Next” button continues the process.
page_review.first_impression: The layout is clear and not crowded. I can easily match each box to what I know about Linh and Bà Nội.

walkthrough.q1_would_try: Yes, I would enter the family details now.
walkthrough.q2_notice_control: Yes, the labelled text boxes, drop-down lists and orange “Next” button are easy to notice.
walkthrough.q3_label_matches_goal: Yes. “Who’s the star of the story?” matches making Linh the hero, and “Who else is in the story?” lets me add Bà Nội. The label asks only for a first name, but I still have the full cultural name “Bà Nội.”

issues.title: No field for the second person's appearance
issues.evidence: [9] “What do they look like? (optional)” appears only beneath the child's section, while [10] asks “Who else is in the story?” with no appearance field.
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: Bà Nội has an important appearance in our memory: a grey bun and purple áo dài. I want the story pictures to show her correctly, not only Linh.
issues.fix: Add an optional “What do they look like?” field under the second-character details, with the same label and help as the child's appearance field.

issues.title: The character name label may restrict Vietnamese names
issues.evidence: [10] “Who else is in the story?” and its placeholder says “e.g. Grandma Rose,” with no indication that a full or culturally meaningful name is welcome.
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I need to preserve the exact Vietnamese name “Bà Nội.” The English example may make me worry the site will change it.
issues.fix: Rename the field to “Character's name” and use a culturally neutral example such as “e.g. Bà Nội or Grandma Rose.”

positives: The heading clearly says Linh will be the star.
The age and pronoun choices include age 4 and “she / her.”
The “Next” button has a clear, simple label.
The form avoids technical instructions and asks only for relevant details.

output.memory_note: Enter Linh, age 4, she/her, long black hair with a red ribbon and round cheeks. Enter Bà Nội as a Grandparent.
output.plan: I will fill in Linh's details, add Bà Nội, and click “Next” to continue creating the story.

title: Create your book – StoryHearth

output.observation: The story setup has moved to a “Choose the look & feel” step. I can select a reading level and illustration style, with “Lexile 200L–500L” and “Watercolour — soft and dreamy” currently selected, then continue with “Next”.
output.think_aloud: The layout is clear, but I do not know what “Lexile” means. Because Linh is four, I think the youngest range, “Lexile BR–200L,” is safer. The watercolour pictures look gentle and nice, so I will keep that and continue.
output.last_action_feedback: partly: The new “Choose the look & feel” screen clearly shows that “Next” worked, but it did not warn me that more than 200 characters had been removed from my story before I continued.

page_review.purpose: Choose how easy the finished story should be to read and what the illustrations should look like.
page_review.what_is_happening: The page shows four reading-level choices and three illustration styles. One reading level and one illustration style are selected, with Back and Next buttons below.
page_review.first_impression: The page looks calm and the choices are easy to see. However, “Lexile” is a technical reading term that I do not understand.

walkthrough.q1_would_try: Yes, because Linh is four and I want a story that will be easy for her age.
walkthrough.q2_notice_control: Yes, I notice the four reading-level radio buttons and the three illustration-style radio buttons.
walkthrough.q3_label_matches_goal: Only partly. The illustration labels clearly describe the look, but the Lexile numbers do not clearly tell me which level is right for a four-year-old.

issues.title: Reading levels use an unexplained technical scale
issues.evidence: “Reading level” followed by “Lexile BR–200L,” “Lexile 200L–500L,” “Lexile 500L–800L,” and “Lexile 800L+”
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I know Linh reads at age four, but the numbers do not help me understand what story level she needs.
issues.fix: Show plain-language labels such as “For ages 0–4 (beginning reader)” and put the Lexile score in smaller supporting text.

issues.title: Age four is not matched clearly
issues.evidence: “Lexile 200L–500L” is checked by default, even though the supplied child age is 4.
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I cannot tell if the default is right for Linh, and I do not want to make the story too difficult for her.
issues.fix: Recommend the age-four level automatically and explain why, while still allowing me to change it.

positives: The page has one clear purpose: choosing the reading level and illustration style.
The selected radio buttons are visually clear.
The illustration descriptions are easy to understand.
There are clear “Back” and “Next” buttons.

new_issues.title: The story text was silently cut to 200 characters
new_issues.evidence: The previous action reported that the story box “now only shows 200 characters; the end of what you typed was cut off”
new_issues.why_it_matters_to_me: The end of our family memory may be missing, including details that make the story personal and correct.
new_issues.fix: Show the character limit before typing, keep the full text internally, and ask for confirmation before continuing if any content was removed.

output.memory_note: Choose the beginning-reader reading level for Linh because she is four. The previous story input was silently shortened to 200 characters.
output.plan: I will select “Lexile BR–200L” because Linh is four, keep the gentle watercolour style, and click “Next” to continue. I will also carefully check the finished story for any missing memory details.

output.observation: The Pricing page lists three products: a free digital preview, a $24.99 hardcover book with 20 glossy pages, and a $4.99 new story version. output.think_aloud: Now I can see the hardcover price: $24.99. This is clear, but I am worried because my online story has only 9 pages while the hardcover says 20 pages. I also need to know if £ conversion, postage, and tax are extra before I understand the real cost.

page_review.purpose: Show the cost of the digital preview, hardcover book, and a new generated version.
page_review.what_is_happening: Three pricing cards show Free, $24.99, and $4.99. A “Start your book” button appears below, but there is no control to choose or order the hardcover from this page.
page_review.first_impression: The main prices are easy to read, and $24.99 is better than finding it only at checkout. However, the 20-page description does not explain why my generated book has only 9 pages, and I cannot tell what the final delivered price will be.

issues.title: Possible extra charges are not explained
issues.evidence: "Hardcover book $24.99" and "20 glossy pages, printed and bound to last."
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I am in England and the price is in dollars. I need to know if this is the final cost or if postage, tax, currency conversion, or other charges will be added.
issues.fix: Show the currency clearly and state whether the price includes tax and shipping. If extra charges may apply, say so before checkout and give a clear example.

issues.title: The advertised page count does not match my book
issues.evidence: The hardcover says "20 glossy pages," but my generated online book has 9 pages.
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I would worry that I would receive a different book or extra pages I did not expect, or that some part of my story could be lost.
issues.fix: Explain how the 9-page story becomes 20 printed pages, or advertise the page count that matches the selected book.

issues.title: No way to order the current book from pricing
issues.evidence: The only button is [6] "Start your book"; the "Hardcover book" card is not a control.
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I already made a book and do not want to start another one. I need a clear route to inspect the final order for Linh’s existing book.
issues.fix: Add an “Order this book” button for each existing book, or direct me to the current book’s order page.

issues.title: Footer text has very low contrast
issues.evidence: The footer labels "Privacy," "Terms," and "Contact" appear very pale against the background.
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I can hardly read these links, so I cannot easily check how my family information and order are handled.
issues.fix: Use darker text and a clearly visible focus or hover state that meets accessible contrast requirements.

page_review.purpose: Review the hardcover order price, delivery cost, and any extras before entering an address and paying.
page_review.what_is_happening: The page has opened the payment step for “The Magical Adventure of Linh.” A countdown says the price is reserved for 09:57. The hardcover, pre-selected gift wrap, shipping, total, address field, and card fields are shown.

issues.title: Gift wrap is selected by default
issues.evidence: checkbox "Premium gift wrap" (checked), £7.99
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I might accidentally pay £7.99 for something I did not choose, and I worry about unexpected costs.
issues.fix: Make every optional extra unchecked by default and label it clearly as an optional add-on. Show how the total changes when it is selected or removed.

issues.title: The displayed total does not identify tax
issues.evidence: “Total £45.97” with no separate VAT or tax line
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I need to know whether the shown total is the amount I will actually be charged.
issues.fix: Show whether tax is included in the total, or itemise VAT and any other required charges before checkout.

issues.title: The currency changed without explanation

issues.title: The full cost is learned only after ordering
issues.evidence: The £7.99 gift wrap and £12.99 shipping & handling first appear on the Checkout page.
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I cannot compare the complete value before choosing “Order hardcover.”
issues.fix: Show the starting total for delivery and any optional extras on the pricing page or book page before checkout.

positives: The hardcover, gift wrap, shipping, and total each have clear prices.
The currency and total are shown together, so the arithmetic is easy to understand.
There is no need to enter payment information to see the current total.

output.plan: I will uncheck “Premium gift wrap” to see the hardcover and delivery cost without the extra item. I will not complete delivery or payment fields.

title: Checkout – StoryHearth

output.observation: The checkout now shows the gift wrap checkbox as unchecked, and the total has fallen from £45.97 to £37.98. The cost is £24.99 for the hardcover plus £12.99 shipping and handling, with no tax shown.
output.think_aloud: Good, the site clearly showed that removing gift wrap changed the total. I now know the real cost without gift wrap is £37.98. I will not enter my address or card details, and I will not click “Pay now.”
output.last_action_feedback: yes — the Premium gift wrap checkbox became unchecked and the total immediately changed from £45.97 to £37.98.

new_issues.title: Removed gift-wrap price still looks active
new_issues.evidence: After [6] “Premium gift wrap” is unchecked, “£7.99” remains beside it without being crossed out or labelled as removed.
new_issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I understand the new total, but the separate £7.99 line looks as if it may still be included. I need clear proof that gift wrap costs nothing in this order.
new_issues.fix: When the checkbox is unchecked, cross out the £7.99 price and label it “Not included,” or remove the line completely.

new_issues.title: Very short reservation timer creates pressure
new_issues.evidence: The message says, “Your price is reserved for 09:42.”
new_issues.why_it_matters_to_me: Nine minutes makes me feel that I must hurry and enter payment quickly. I need to compare the cost carefully, not feel forced.
new_issues.fix: Remove the timer, or explain the exact condition and give a longer reasonable reservation period without linking it to a payment prompt.

output.memory_note: Final hardcover checkout cost without gift wrap: £37.98 (£24.99 hardcover + £12.99 shipping and handling). No tax shown. Do not pay.
output.plan: I have completed my check of the full price. I will stop here without entering any personal, address, or payment information.
